questions.stem: Why can synapses only transmit impulses in one direction?

options.text: Because neurones only have one axon
Because neurotransmitters are only released from one side and receptors are only on the other side
Because the myelin sheath blocks backward transmission
Because electrical impulses can only travel in one direction

questions.explanation: Neurotransmitter vesicles are only found on the pre-synaptic side, and the receptors for these chemicals are only on the post-synaptic membrane. This ensures impulses travel in one direction only.
